metadata.note: PART 2 of 2. Companion to weekly_updates/08-14(2)/ ('From The Crawl To The Conversation'), which covered the BUILD half of the author's LLM-lifecycle blog post. This reel is the DEPLOYMENT half that was deliberately dropped there to hold ~120s: inference knobs, quantization, LoRA/QLoRA, and choosing a model by cheapest cost per successful task. Together the two reels cover the whole post. THROUGH-LINE: everything after training is a cost decision — memory, latency, dollars — and the discipline is to buy capability only where it changes the answer. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW: every figure is the author's own — 7B at 32-bit = 28 GB, half precision 14 GB, INT8 7 GB, INT4 3.5 GB, error per value ~1e-7 to ~1e-1, asymmetric scale = (x_max - x_min) / (q_max - q_min), LoRA W' = W + BA with B of d×r and A of r×k, the 3×3 rank-1 example giving 6 trainable numbers instead of 9, QLoRA = adapters on a frozen 4-bit base putting 7B fine-tuning on one consumer GPU, output tokens several times the price of input tokens, a naive N-step agentic loop growing roughly quadratically. NOTHING is invented. B04's counts (9 and 6) are DERIVED by the component from d/k/r rather than passed in, so the numbers cannot contradict the matrices drawn beside them. B02 uses ScaleComparison, which is a numeric pattern — legitimate here because all four memory values are real; the band is labelled only for the 4-bit case the blog actually makes a claim about. ILLUSTRATE LAW: Claude UI at B00, B07, B08, B09 only; the six body beats are InferenceKnobs -> ScaleComparison -> BinaryBranch -> LoraFactorization -> DivergentFates -> ChipGrid, all distinct. NEW TEMPLATES: LlmInferenceKnobs and LlmLoraFactorization (runtime/remotion/src/LlmDeployIllu.tsx). BRANDING RULE 7: slot-1 kicker stays 'Computational Skepticism'.
